trust_decision.summary: When httpc follows a 3xx automatically, httpc_response:redirect/2 decides which credentials from the original request (record headers, URL userinfo) go with the follow-up request to the new host:port. At the pinned commit it copies all of them unconditionally.

landing_point.why: The summary says the Authorization header leaks on redirect. redirect/2 is the only function that builds the redirected request, and it copies Request#request.headers into NewHeaders.

fix_sites.entry_point: httpc:request/1,2,4,5 with autoredirect=true (default), reached via httpc_response:result/2 for 300/301/302/303/307/308 (lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc_response.erl:112-144)
fix_sites.module_kind: core response handler (only changed source site; one function, one hunk covering header-record stripping and clearing userinfo)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc_request.erl:285-299 (handle_user_info/2, called on every send at lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc_request.erl:86). This is the URL-userinfo producer. The published fix closes it by clearing #request.userinfo in redirect/2 (fix.diff:109-119).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report talks about the Authorization header. A solver who strips that header in redirect/2 and tests with an explicit header sees it gone. The user:pass@host URL form produces no header in the record: send/4 rebuilds Authorization from #request.userinfo in another module, so the fix looks complete. The upstream fix commit itself calls this a 'missed codepath'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Same-origin redirects (same host and port) must keep Authorization and userinfo credentials. Proxy-Authorization from the proxy_auth option is rebuilt per send for the proxy and must keep working. Cookie-jar cookies for the new host are added by httpc_manager:handle_cookies after the redirect and must still be sent. Over-broad fixes break these: stripping on every redirect, disabling cookie handling on redirect, or dropping proxy_auth.

O6_input_shapes: explicit authorization header in the user header list (record field, lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc.erl:1860-1862)

cookie / origin headers held in #http_request_h.other (catch-all, lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc.erl:1946-1950); this includes the jar cookie that httpc_manager:handle_cookies prepends (lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc_manager.erl:910)
URL userinfo user:pass@host and user@host (no password), which become Basic auth at lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc_request.erl:288-296
user header names in any case (lowercased at lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc.erl:1159 before the record is built)

O7_producer.where: lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc_request.erl:285-299 (handle_user_info builds Authorization from #request.userinfo at send time). Also lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc_manager.erl:898-912 (cookie-jar header put into headers.other before the first send, so it is carried in the record that redirect/2 copies).

O8_uncovered_routes.route: With the headers_as_is=true request option, send/4 transmits the user's raw header list (#request.headers_as_is), not the header record. redirect/2 never touches that field, so Authorization/Cookie/Proxy-Authorization in the raw list still reach the cross-origin target after the published fix.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The docs call headers_as_is a workaround 'only if there is no other way ... or for testing purpose' and say no headers are automatically added (lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc.erl:343-348), so a solver can argue a raw-pass-through mode is the user's responsibility.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same package, different file (httpc_request.erl post_data/4 and update_headers/4 at lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc_request.erl:241-242; field set at lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc.erl:1210, 1343-1349)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The published cross-origin test compares only {Host,Port} (fix.diff:82). An https->http redirect to the same host with an explicit identical port counts as same-origin and keeps credentials, although RFC 9110 origin includes the scheme.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Default ports differ by scheme, so a scheme change almost always changes the port too. A solver can call same-port scheme downgrade an exotic configuration.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-profile default credential option (e.g. a {basic_auth, {U,P}} http_option analogous to proxy_auth) that send/4 rebuilds into Authorization on every send, from #request.settings rather than headers or userinfo
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: proxy_auth already follows exactly this pattern (option -> header rebuilt at send time), so a maintainer adding origin auth would copy it. Clearing headers in redirect/2 would not stop it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A handler-level redirect shortcut (e.g. pipelined/keep-alive redirect reuse) that rebuilds #request from the old one without going through httpc_response:redirect/2
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The handler already rewrites requests on retry/redirect and on the ipfamily interpolation path (lib/inets/src/http_client/httpc_handler.erl:1083-1087), so a second request-cloning helper is plausible.

O9_family: CWE-601-adjacent credential forwarding on cross-origin redirect (sensitive header / userinfo leak via HTTP client auto-redirect)

O10_build.toolchain: Erlang/OTP source build (autoconf, make, C compiler for erts); alternatively a matching prebuilt OTP 27 with inets recompiled
O10_build.project_tests: lib/inets/test/httpc_SUITE.erl (common_test). Uses in-process simulated HTTP servers (only_simulated group) on localhost, e.g. existing redirect_* cases.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Set authorization = undefined in NewHeaders in redirect/2 on host change, leaving userinfo, cookie/origin in .other, proxy-authorization, referer and headers_as_is untouched.

out_of_scope_notes: httpc_manager:handle_cookies prepends a jar cookie header on every handle_request, including same-origin redirects, so the cookie header may be duplicated (not a cross-origin leak).
unverified: Presence in latest release not checked (no latest tree provided).

The fix's test relies on a sim-server path capture_sensitive_redirect_target.html and a url/4 helper with userinfo that do not appear in the diff hunks shown. Where they live, and whether they already exist at the pinned commit, was not checked.
No second HTTP client implementation in other OTP apps was searched exhaustively; only lib/inets/src/http_client was examined.
Whether a proxied request (address =/= SendAddr) changes the cross-origin comparison was not traced.
